Causal forests

Source: vignettes/grf.Rmd
grf.Rmd

Use grf_cate() and grf_crr() to fit treatment-effect models with the grf package. Pass your data directly, with optional nuisance estimates. Both functions return an hte3_model with predict() and summary() methods.

library(hte3)

Choose the target

  • Use grf_cate() when the target is a conditional mean difference.
  • Use grf_crr() when the target is a conditional risk ratio and the outcome is non-negative.

Choose a CATE method

grf_cate() supports method = c("dr", "r", "ep").

  • method = "r" trains grf::causal_forest().
  • method = "dr" uses the DR-learner with GRF nuisance and base learners.
  • method = "ep" uses the EP-learner with GRF nuisance and base learners.

Within the EP family, ep_targeting_style = "dr" selects EP-DR and ep_targeting_style = "r" selects EP-R. If you pass ep_targeting_style = c("dr", "r"), cross-validation can compare both EP variants.

If you omit both method and cross_validate, grf_cate() compares the default EP-R candidate and the GRF causal forest.

data <- hte3_example_data(n = 200, seed = 1)

fit <- grf_cate(
  data = data,
  modifiers = c("W1", "W2"),
  confounders = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  treatment = "A",
  outcome = "Y",
  method = "r",
  cross_fit = FALSE
)

head(predict(fit, data))
summary(fit)

grf_crr()

grf_crr() supports method = c("ep", "ipw", "t"). If you omit method, the wrapper fits one EP model.

fit <- grf_crr(
  data = data,
  modifiers = c("W1", "W2"),
  confounders = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  treatment = "A",
  outcome = "Y_binary",
  method = "ep",
  cross_fit = FALSE
)

head(predict(fit, data))
summary(fit)

Supply nuisance estimates

The GRF wrappers accept direct nuisance estimates:

  • mu.hat: an n x 2 matrix ordered as (control, treatment)
  • pi.hat: a length-n vector for P(A = treatment_level | X)
  • m.hat: an optional length-n vector estimating E[Y | X]

If m.hat is omitted and both mu.hat and pi.hat are supplied, hte3 computes m.hat internally.

mu.hat <- cbind(data$mu0, data$mu1)
pi.hat <- data$pi1

fit <- grf_cate(
  data = data,
  modifiers = c("W1", "W2"),
  confounders = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  treatment = "A",
  outcome = "Y",
  mu.hat = mu.hat,
  pi.hat = pi.hat,
  cross_fit = FALSE
)

Tuning and cross-validation

Use these arguments to control the fit:

  • cross_fit and folds for nuisance estimation
  • cross_validate and cv_control for outer learner selection
  • ep_targeting_style and ep_r_targeting_basis for the EP variants
  • treatment_level and control_level when treatment labels are not the default 1 and 0
  • grf_params for GRF hyperparameters such as num.trees or min.node.size
  • tune for the amount of GRF tuning: "light", "none", or "all"

In the GRF learners, tune = "light" tunes sample.fraction, mtry, and min.node.size with a modest search budget. tune = "none" disables tuning, and tune = "all" tunes all parameters supported by GRF.

Supported treatments and outcomes

  • grf_cate() and grf_crr() currently support binary treatment only.
  • grf_crr() requires a non-negative outcome.
  • For continuous-treatment CATE, use hte_task() and fit_cate(..., method = "r").

Construct learners directly

Use these helpers to construct GRF learners for a custom sl3 model library or manual cross-validation:

  • make_grf_base_learner()
  • make_grf_nuisance_learners()
  • make_grf_cate_learners()
  • make_grf_crr_learners()
